title: Case-goods brand importing Chinese bedroom furniture into New Jersey

input.what: Case-goods brand importing Chinese bedroom furniture

assumptions: A brand importing wooden bedroom furniture made in China through Newark, with no store (the seller path). Company and tax filings as nj-dresser-importer.json. Chinese wooden bedroom furniture is under the antidumping order A-570-890 and Section 301's List 3. Dressers aren't named, so the clothing storage unit rule isn't claimed; nothing upholstered is named.

items.name: Certificate of formation
items.agency: NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services
items.match: certificate of formation|business formation|nj-formation|public records filing
items.quote: First, file a Certificate of formation/authorization.
items.note: Fee wording on the page is ambiguous for LLCs; not scored.

items.name: Employer Identification Number (EIN)
items.quote: You never have to pay a fee for an EIN.
items.feeQuote: You never have to pay a fee for an EIN.

items.name: Tax and employer registration (Form NJ-REG)
items.agency: NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services
items.quote: Second, after filing the certificate of formation/authorization, file the tax/employer registration form (Form NJ-REG).

items.name: Importer identity (CBP Form 5106)
items.note: Filed with the first formal entry or request for services (19 CFR 24.5).

items.name: Customs bond (CBP Form 301)
items.note: Merchandise isn't released at entry without a single or continuous bond (19 CFR 142.4(a)); the port director may waive it at $2,500 or less.
items.quote: unless a single entry or continuous bond on Customs Form 301, containing the bond conditions set forth in § 113.62 of this chapter,

items.name: Importer Security Filing (ISF, 10+2)
items.quote: later than 24 hours before the cargo is laden aboard the vessel at the foreign port.
items.condition: Furniture arriving by ocean (19 CFR 149.2(a)); CBP's own pages refuse automated reads, so the regulation is read on GovInfo.

items.name: ACE Secure Data Portal account
items.quote: register an entity as an Importer of Record (IOR) in the Automated Commercial Environment (ACE)
items.condition: An importer of record sees its entries, duties and bond in ACE.

items.name: Lacey Act declaration (PPQ Form 505)
items.quote: Importers should have a copy of the form available for CBP to review at the port of entry.

items.name: TSCA Title VI import certification
items.quote: Importers to provide import certification under TSCA beginning March 22, 2019;

items.name: Product safety certificate (eFiling)
items.note: The library's general certificate row abstains (no current quote); the clothing storage unit certificate is scored as cpsc-1261.

order.quote: The ISF Importer must possess a basic importation and entry bond
order.why: 19 CFR 149.5(b): the ISF importer holds a bond (or the agent posts its own) for the filing.

order.quote: later than 24 hours before the cargo is laden aboard the vessel at the foreign port.
order.why: The ISF goes in before the cargo is loaded abroad; the Lacey Act declaration is made at entry.
